newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria PM urges wage cuts to meet IMF targets.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria PM urges wage cuts to meet IMF targets.

text.p: Bulgaria's Prime Minister Ivan Kostov urged the country's biggest refinery Neftochim to cut monthly wages in line with International Monetary Fund recommendations to curb budget spending and deficit.

"The Prime Minister demanded from Neftochim's management to reduce monthly wages to the level complying with the draft budget frame and public sector wage regulation mechanism," the government said in a statement.

Average monthly wages in Neftochim were raised from 165,000 ($83) levs in February to 480,000 levs ($320) in April, while the refinery's dues to the state on May 29 amounted to 73 billion levs ($47 million), said the statement.

Kostov also criticised the unjustifiably high wages in the National Electricity Company, which pledged to seek through courts its dues from companies not paying their electricity bills, said the statement.

The IMF and the Bulgarian government have so far failed to agree the size of 1997 budget deficit. The IMF envisages reducing budget deficit in 1997 to 3.8 percent from 10.9 percent last year by eliminating the need for central bank credit to the government and rationalising expenditures.

The Fund extended its mission to Bulgaria to narrow down the deficit in this year's draft budget, after finding that the estimated deficit is larger than recommended. Latest budget-frame figures have not been published so far.

The IMF slammed the government for raising wages higher than the planned $75 per month by year-end and for concentrating most of the pay-raises in power-engineering, the national airline and few state banks.
After adjustments to inflation and depreciation of the national currency, average state wages have risen from $30 per month to between $100 and $400 monthly in the past several months.
